evidence: createHttpServer only registers Express routes (app.post/app.get/app.patch) and passes work to service.addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, advanceOrder and cancelOrder: transport work.
stringValue and the inline typeof/Array.isArray checks in the /products and /orders handlers check the shape of the request body. This is HTTP input parsing, not a domain rule.

The GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state handlers check membership in the domain's orderStates list but do not decide whether a state transition is allowed. That decision is left to service.advanceOrder.
The error middleware maps DomainError and NotFoundError to 400 and 404, and anything else to 500. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes is presentation/transport work.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is an Express HTTP adapter in the infrastructure layer. Its jobs are to register routes, check that request bodies and query parameters have the right shape, call the FulfilmentService application methods, and turn errors into HTTP status codes. All of these are transport and framework tasks that belong in infrastructure. The checks only confirm that inputs have the right type, and that the order state is a known value from the domain's orderStates list. That is input parsing, not a business rule. Business rules would be things like stock levels, allowed state transitions or cancellation rules, and all of those are left to the service and domain. One small point: the code uses DomainError for input-shape errors, and the error messages repeat the list of state names. Both are minor coupling, not business logic placed in the wrong layer.
